task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Operational definition of 'PULL_UP' as a counter
Statistical methods for comparing outcomes across units
Identifying confounding variables in strategic analysis
Establishing causal links between sequential plays

historical_evidence.finding: PBP-derived shot-level PNR rates sit in a realistic band (script notes possession-level rates will be higher) and vary by team as expected. 2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots ranges from OKC 7.567% to IND 13.824%.
R1 TOV-force channel lifts shrink ~50%+ after opponent re-route or PT-shift (R2) and follow-the-ball counter (R3). Net lift is model-implied, not observed in the games.

Hypothesis that each engine layer (PNR calibration, scheme fingerprint, tier correction, sequential conditioning) improves prediction of observed series PPP was rejected. No forward config beats V0_NEUTRAL (all beat rates <0.5); placebo ties or beats V4 in the first version.
The system's offensive strategy marginally beat actual team strategies (+1.16 pts/100). Equilibrium PPP is model-implied not observed.

failed_approaches.why: Net lift is model-implied, not observed in the games; R3 often additive surrogate at n<10.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Engine layers for predicting series PPP
failed_approaches.why: No forward config beats V0_NEUTRAL (all beat rates <0.5, CI excludes 0.5 above); placebo ties or beats V4 in the first version. (adequately powered null result)
Doc verdict 'MARGINAL'; equilibrium PPP is model-implied not observed.

evidence_establishes: PNR plays and shots can be identified from play-by-play data ([prior work][prior work]).
The concept of 'lift' as offensive efficiency (e.g., PPP) is a relevant measure in basketball analytics ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
Model-implied outcomes for offensive efficiency have been used in prior work, though sometimes with limitations or inconclusive results ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: A clear, established operational definition for 'PNR fail'.
A standard method for identifying a 'PULL_UP' as a direct counter to a 'PNR fail'.
How to measure 'lift' for a specific sequential play-type combination (PNR fail -> PULL_UP).
A definition for 'units' in the context of league-wide counter strategy analysis.
Whether league-wide counter strategies have been successfully identified and quantified with observed (not model-implied) 'lift' in prior research.
own_inferences: The available play-by-play and derived play-type data should allow for identification of PNR plays and pull-up shots.

A precise operational definition of 'PNR fail' is crucial and would likely involve a PNR possession that does not yield an immediate positive outcome (e.g., shot by PNR handler/roller, foul drawn) or results in a negative outcome (e.g., turnover, poor shot).
A 'PULL_UP as a counter' would need to be defined as a pull-up shot occurring within a short, defined temporal window after a 'PNR fail' on the same possession or immediate subsequent possession.

'Lift' would likely be measured as points per possession (PPP) or effective field goal percentage (eFG%) for these 'counter' PULL_UP shots, compared to a baseline of PULL_UP shots not following a PNR fail, or compared to the PNR fail outcome itself.
'Units' most likely refer to specific player combinations or individual players, requiring sufficient sample size for each to assess 'lift'.
uncertainties: The exact operational definitions for 'PNR fail' and 'PULL_UP as a counter' are not provided.
The methodology for establishing a baseline for 'lift' and for comparing it across units is not specified.
Potential confounding factors (e.g., defensive scheme, game state, player skill, shot clock situation) need to be controlled for.
The feasibility of achieving sufficient sample size for 'units' (e.g., specific player combinations) to reliably calculate lift and test the 70% threshold and 2pp median lift criteria.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence highlighted that previous studies often relied on model-implied outcomes for 'lift' ([prior work][prior work], [prior work][prior work]) and that predictive models of offensive efficiency can fail against simple baselines or placebos ([prior work][prior work]). This reinforces the need for a robust, observed-data-driven definition of 'lift' and a strong control or baseline for comparison, as well as acknowledging the difficulty in establishing clear 'lift' in complex strategic scenarios. It also showed that PNR identification from PBP is feasible ([prior work][prior work]), which is a positive.

blocking_constraints.text: The specific sequence of 'PNR fail' followed by a 'PULL_UP counter' might be rare for many specific units, leading to insufficient sample sizes to reliably calculate 'lift' and meet the '>=70% of units' criteria.
Defining 'PNR fail' and 'PULL_UP as a counter' robustly from play-by-play data, especially distinguishing a 'counter' from a generic pull-up, can be challenging and subject to measurement error.

Many factors influence shot selection and success, making it difficult to isolate the 'lift' attributable solely to the PNR fail -> PULL_UP counter sequence. Game state, defensive pressure, player matchups, and shot clock are major confounders.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved historical evidence directly answers the question of whether PNR failure leads to a league-wide PULL_UP counter with specific lift thresholds. Previous work has touched on PNR identification, offensive efficiency (PPP/lift), and adversarial strategies, but not this specific sequence and outcome.

risks.text: The specific sequence of 'PNR fail' followed by a 'PULL_UP counter' might be infrequent, particularly at the unit level, making it difficult to achieve sufficient observations for statistical significance and to meet the '>=70% of units' requirement. This is especially true for the 'median lift > 2pp' criterion, which requires stable estimates for each unit.

The operational definitions of 'PNR fail' and 'PULL_UP as a counter' are critical. A 'PNR fail' needs to be clearly distinguishable from any PNR possession that doesn't end in a direct PNR score. A 'PULL_UP counter' needs to be clearly linked causally or temporally to the PNR fail, and not just a subsequent unrelated play. Errors in these definitions could lead to misclassification and unreliable 'lift' measurements.

Many variables could influence both the occurrence of a 'PNR fail' and the subsequent 'PULL_UP' outcome. These include defensive scheme, game situation (score, quarter, time on clock), individual player skill, and shot clock pressure. Without careful controls, observed 'lift' might be attributed to the counter-strategy when it's actually due to these confounders.

Meeting the '>=70% of units' and 'median lift > 2pp' criteria requires adequate power for each unit's lift calculation. Given the potential sparsity of events, many units might not have enough data to reliably estimate their 'lift' above 0 or 2pp. The definition of 'unit' (e.g., individual player, specific lineup) will heavily impact this risk.

If 'units' are defined as many individual players or player combinations, testing the 'lift>0' hypothesis for each unit (to determine the >=70% threshold) will involve multiple comparisons, increasing the risk of false positives without appropriate correction.

design.estimand: The 'lift' in Points Per Possession (PPP) or Effective Field Goal Percentage (eFG%) of PULL_UP shots that occur within 4 seconds of a 'PNR fail' event initiated by the same offensive player, compared to the PPP/eFG% of PULL_UP shots not preceded by a 'PNR fail' (baseline). The estimand is whether this lift is >0 in >=70% of identified units (player-initiators) with a median lift >2pp across those units, league-wide.
design.unit: Each individual offensive player who initiates both PNR plays and PULL_UP shots. A 'unit' is defined as a unique player.
design.sample: All NBA regular season and playoff games from 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (complete seasons). Data will be filtered to include only half-court possessions. 'PNR fail' is defined as a PNR possession that results in either a turnover, a contested shot with <24% eFG%, or a shot clock violation, where the PNR ball handler or roller does not take the shot. A 'PULL_UP counter' is defined as a pull-up shot taken by the same PNR ball handler within 4 seconds of a 'PNR fail' event.
design.power: A minimum of 50 'PNR fail -> PULL_UP counter' possessions and 200 'baseline PULL_UP' possessions per player unit will be required to be included in the '>=70% of units' assessment. Power analysis will be conducted to determine the detectable effect size for a 2pp lift with alpha=0.05 and beta=0.2 for each unit. Units not meeting the minimum sample size will be excluded from the 70% calculation.
design.controls: Statistical controls for confounding variables will include: game state (score differential, quarter), time remaining on shot clock, defensive pressure (contested shot indicator), and player fixed effects. A matched-sample or regression-based approach will be considered to compare 'counter' PULL_UPs to 'baseline' PULL_UPs by controlling for these factors. Baseline PULL_UPs will be defined as all other PULL_UP shots by the same player in similar game situations.
design.falsification: The null hypothesis is that 'lift' is <=0 for PULL_UP shots following a PNR fail, or that fewer than 70% of units show lift>0, or that the median lift across units is <=2pp. A falsification test could involve comparing the lift of PULL_UPs after PNR fail to PULL_UPs after *successful* PNR plays, expecting no significant lift or even a negative lift in the latter case.
design.multiplicity: For the 'lift>0 in >=70% of units' criterion, a False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (e.g., Benjamini-Hochberg) will be applied to the p-values for individual unit 'lift > 0' tests. The median lift calculation will be performed on the raw lift values for all units meeting the power threshold.
design.decision_rule: The hypothesis is supported if: (1) At least 70% of player units (meeting minimum sample size requirements) show a statistically significant 'lift' > 0 (p < 0.05 after FDR correction), AND (2) The median 'lift' across all such qualified player units is > 2 points per possession (or equivalent eFG%).
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 complete seasons (regular season and playoffs). Derived play-type possession records from [source] database.
